channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Promises Aid in Nephrologist's Case
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov has pledged to assist in the case of nephrologist Nasira Beishebaeva. During a regional visit, residents requested the president's intervention. The doctor was convicted and sentenced for her role in a patient's leg amputation. The president stated, "Then we will help."

item.title: Russian Airstrikes Kill 55 in Ukraine's Kamyshevakha; Energy Infrastructure Targeted
item.description: Russian airstrikes on the front-line village of Kamyshevakha in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region have increased the death toll to 55. The State Emergency Service of Ukraine reported that nine more bodies were found under rubble. The attacks on November 2 targeted a humanitarian aid distribution point and a shelter. Russia also launched massive strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure on November 7, causing power outages in several regions.

item.title: Iran Executes Three Men Accused of Attacking Public Infrastructure
item.description: Iran has executed three men identified as Hassan Dehband, Hamid Kazemi, and Reza Zanganeh. They were accused of attacking public infrastructure, including an electricity substation, and acting in the interests of Israel and the United States during recent protests.

item.title: Kazakhstan Currency Exchange Rates on November 8
item.description: On November 8, the exchange rates for the US dollar, Euro, and Russian Ruble in Kazakhstan's exchange offices were as follows: Astana - USD (buy 446, sell 453), EUR (buy 499, sell 509), RUB (buy 5.15, sell 5.35). Almaty and Shymkent rates also varied.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Defining Boundaries Between Faith and Law in Religious Discourse
item.description: Kazakhstan is navigating the complex line between religious freedom and legal boundaries, particularly concerning online sermons and spiritual marriages. Experts emphasize that violating Kazakh laws is the primary criterion for distinguishing radicalism from conservatism in religious expression.

item.title: Tajikistan's Agricultural Output Rises 8.5% to 67.1 Billion Somoni
item.description: Agricultural production in Tajikistan increased by 8.5% to 67.1 billion somoni in January-September 2026 compared to the same period last year. The Ministry of Agriculture reported growth driven by increased cultivation of potatoes, vegetables, field crops, and grapes, alongside livestock and other agricultural products.

item.title: New 220/110/10 kV Substation to Enhance Dushanbe's Power Supply
item.description: A new 220/110/10 kV electrical substation is planned near Dushanbe, aiming to improve the reliability of electricity supply to the capital and surrounding areas. The project, funded by the Tajik government and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), is part of the 2022–2030 energy sector development plan. Construction is scheduled for completion by August 2028.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Sets Maximum Retail Prices for Coal for the Public
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has established maximum retail prices for coal sold to the public, ranging from 4,100 to 12,100 soms per ton depending on the region, coal grade, and origin. These state-regulated prices will be in effect until January 18, 2027. The maximum price for a ton of 'Kara-Keche' coal in Bishkek is set at 7,000 soms.

item.title: China's Vice Premier Urges Balanced Trade Through Openness and Cooperation
item.description: Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang called for joint efforts to achieve balanced trade by increasing market openness, deepening investment cooperation, promoting innovation, and reducing trade barriers. Speaking at the China International Import Expo, he emphasized the need to address global trade imbalances and expand the economic pie through shared market opportunities and integration into global supply chains.

item.title: Tajikistan and Kazakhstan Sign 20 Cooperation Documents
item.description: Tajikistan and Kazakhstan have signed 20 new cooperation documents covering energy, industry, mining, agriculture, digital technologies, and security. The agreements were finalized following talks between Presidents Emomali Rahmon and Kassym-Jomart Tokayev in Astana, marking a strategic partnership level.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Awards Tajik President Rahmon Top State Honor
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev awarded Tajik President Emomali Rahmon the newly established Order of Khoja Akhmet Yassawi, Kazakhstan's highest state award. The ceremony took place in Astana after high-level negotiations. Rahmon was honored for his significant contribution to strengthening bilateral relations and cooperation between the two nations.

item.title: Herat Terminal Power Cut Over Unpaid Electricity Debts by Contracting Company
item.description: The Taliban-controlled Electricity Company in Herat has cut power to the former bus terminal due to unpaid debts by the contracting company. Passengers, shopkeepers, and hotel owners face difficulties. The contracting company owes nearly 20 million Afghanis in electricity bills from the past five years. Power will not be restored until the debt is paid.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Orders Medical Assistance for Two-Year-Old Girl
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has instructed the Minister of Health to provide necessary medical assistance to a two-year-old girl from Chuy region. The child requires treatment in China due to complications following multiple surgeries.

item.title: UN Agencies Report Over Half of Afghan Children Lack Formal Education
item.description: UNESCO and UNICEF stated that more than half of primary school-age children in Afghanistan are deprived of formal education. They warned that continued restrictions on girls' and women's education will hinder future reconstruction and development. Since the Taliban's return, over 2.6 million girls have been barred from attending classes above sixth grade.

item.title: Half of Last Glacier in Algoy Alps Melted Due to Heatwave
item.description: The Schwarzmilzferner glacier in the Algoy Alps has lost its status due to this summer's heatwave, thinning by over 4 meters and losing nearly half its volume. Glaciologist Christoph Mayer predicts its complete disappearance next summer. Glaciers in the Eastern Alps may vanish by 2060-2070, with four German glaciers also at risk.

item.title: New "Halqa" Substation Enhances Power Supply Reliability in Tashkent Region
item.description: A new 500 kV "Halqa" substation was commissioned in the Tashkent region on November 7, improving electricity supply reliability for the capital and parts of the region. The World Bank-supported project, costing $171.4 million, includes 285 km of new high-voltage transmission lines.

item.title: Afghanistan and Iran Discuss Boosting Trade and Investment Ties
item.description: Afghanistan and Iran have held talks to expand bilateral trade, improve cross-border commerce, and create new investment opportunities. Discussions focused on strengthening economic cooperation, streamlining trade procedures, and removing barriers. Both sides agreed to follow up on issues raised and improve coordination between economic institutions.

item.title: Turkish Police Arrest 63 Afghan Citizens and Suspected Migrant Smuggler
item.description: Turkish police have arrested 63 Afghan citizens and a suspected migrant smuggler in Hakkari Province while they were attempting to enter Turkey illegally. The alleged smuggler was sent to prison, and the Afghan citizens will be transferred to Agri Province for legal procedures. The operation aimed to combat migrant smuggling.

item.title: Kazakhstan Eases Restrictions on Foreign Currency Deposit Rates
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deposit Insurance Fund (KFGD) is liberalizing regulations on foreign currency deposit rates. Starting October 1, the maximum rate for new or renewed savings accounts over 12 months has increased from 1% to 2.5% annually. This move is attributed to the successful de-dollarization of the deposit market, with foreign currency deposits falling from 80% in 2015 to 19.2% by September 2026.

item.title: Kazakhstan Vice President Meets with Higgsfield AI Team in Almaty
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice President Yerlan Karin met with the Higgsfield AI team in Almaty, comprising 600 specialists with an average age of 23. Many team members are young Kazakhs who studied or worked abroad and returned specifically for this project. Karin expressed optimism about their contribution to Kazakhstan's international standing in artificial intelligence and innovation.

item.title: Six Dead: Tusk Declares Krakow Shooting a Terrorist Attack
item.description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has declared the shooting incident in Krakow, which resulted in six fatalities, as a terrorist attack. The statement came following the tragic event that has shocked the nation. Further details regarding the investigation and response are expected.

item.title: Krakow Shooting: Death Toll Rises to Nine, Three Found at Attacker's Home
item.description: Polish police have released new details regarding a mass shooting in Krakow, reporting that nine people have died. Three additional bodies were discovered at the suspect's residence, bringing the total fatalities to nine. Two officers were seriously injured during the incident.

item.title: Uzbekistan Weekly: Record Cotton Harvest, Gas Control, Imarat Case, and Migration Rules
item.description: Uzbekistan achieved a record cotton harvest of 5 million tons. Authorities are tightening gas and coal control, identifying hundreds of violations. Over 700 people lost 35 billion soums in Termez due to an auto scam. New migration rules are also in effect.

item.title: Sweden's New Government Formation Stalled After Two Months
item.description: Negotiations to form a new government in Sweden remain ongoing two months after the September 13 parliamentary elections. Political forces have not reached a consensus on the composition of the future government and the distribution of ministerial posts. Public opinion is divided on the ability of Magdalena Andersson to form a government.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Agriculture Minister: Farmers and Clusters Need Each Other for Profit
item.description: Uzbekistan's Minister of Agriculture, Ibrohim Abdurahmonov, views agricultural clusters as the future, emphasizing their need to collaborate with and incentivize farmers. He stated that clusters create a stable market for farmers' produce, particularly cotton, and that neither party can achieve profitability without the other. Textile clusters are seen as the path to market.

item.title: Houthis Claim 33 Killed in Saudi Airstrikes on Village
item.description: Houthi sources claim that 33 people, including women and children, were killed in Saudi Arabian airstrikes on a village. The report does not provide further details on the specific location or context of the attack.

item.title: Uzbek Doctor Saves Passenger's Life on Flight to South Korea
item.description: An Uzbek doctor intervened to save a passenger whose condition rapidly deteriorated on a flight from Uzbekistan to South Korea. Other medical professionals on board also assisted in the critical situation.

item.title: New Olympic Training Base to Be Built in Shchuchinsk, Kazakhstan
item.description: A new Olympic training base for winter sports is under construction in Shchuchinsk, Kazakhstan. The facility will include training jumps, a boarding school for 300 students, and an ice arena for nearly 3,000 spectators, aiming to support athlete development and international competitions.

item.title: US Offers Up to $20 Million Reward for Information on Iran's Nuclear Program
item.description: The U.S. Department of State is offering up to $20 million for information regarding Iran's nuclear program through its "Rewards for Justice" program. The announcement seeks details on facilities, equipment, personnel, and technical aspects. This comes amid ongoing diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions between the US and Iran.

item.title: Iran and US Report Attacks on Three Ships in Strait of Hormuz and Sea of Oman
item.description: Iran and the United States have reported incidents involving attacks on three ships in the Strait of Hormuz and the Sea of Oman. Details regarding the nature of the attacks and the involved parties have been released by both nations.

item.title: Bishkek Schools Add Over 12,000 Students Amid Migration
item.description: Bishkek's schools have seen an influx of 12,500 students this academic year, factoring in internal and external migration, according to Dogdurgul Kendirbaeva. She stated that fifty more schools are needed in Bishkek to address the shortage. The minister noted a significant number of citizens returning from the US and Russia. Currently, 40 schools in Bishkek, Osh, and Manas operate on three shifts.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Agree to Increase Agricultural Trade Turnover
item.description: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan have reached an agreement to boost trade in agricultural products. This deal aims to enhance economic cooperation and increase the exchange of goods between the two nations in the agricultural sector.

item.title: 25 Rescued from Apartment Building Fire in Astana
item.description: Emergency services rescued 25 people, including seven children, from a fire in a multi-story residential building in Astana. The fire, which involved household items in an apartment on the fifth floor, was successfully extinguished by the Ministry of Emergency Situations.

item.title: Germany Cannot Supply More Patriot Systems to Ukraine, Defense Minister Says
item.description: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius stated that Berlin can no longer supply additional Patriot missile defense systems to Ukraine. He explained this decision by the weakening of Germany's own defenses and urged other partner countries to act more proactively.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Banks Sever Ties with Companies Amid Sanctions Risk Mitigation Efforts
item.description: Commercial banks in Kyrgyzstan are actively working to minimize secondary sanctions risks. 'ABank' has terminated business relations with 115 companies, and 'Eldik Bank' has severed ties with 169 organizations deemed high-risk. This coordinated effort aims to comply with international sanctions.

item.title: UN Official Warns ISIS-K Poses Serious Threat to Central, South Asia with New Technologies
item.description: Alexander Zuev, acting head of the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, warned that the Khorasan province branch of the Islamic State (ISIS-K) remains a serious terrorist threat to Central and South Asia. Speaking at the SCO Plus Security meeting in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, he stated that ISIS-K is utilizing drones and artificial intelligence for its activities, acquiring advanced tactical equipment and training. The group exploits instability through its regional branches.

item.title: Kazakhstan NOC President Golovkin Meets IOC Head Coventry in Dakar
item.description: Gennady Golovkin, President of the National Olympic Committee of Kazakhstan, met with IOC President Kirsty Coventry in Dakar. They discussed the development of the Olympic movement and preparations for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games boxing competitions. Kazakhstan has 18 athletes at the Youth Olympics, having won two medals so far.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans 202-Hectare Industrial Zone in Chuy Region
item.description: A new industrial zone spanning 202 hectares is planned for the Chuy region of Kyrgyzstan. The project aims to attract 21 enterprises with an estimated investment of 31.64 billion soms. Infrastructure development will require 600 million soms, according to President Sadyr Japarov.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Constructs 34.9 km of Irrigation Canals in Chuy Region
item.description: In the Chuy region, 34.9 kilometers of irrigation canals have been built, repaired, and cleaned as part of efforts to improve water supply. Additionally, 44.78 km of water pipelines were installed between 2021 and 2026, according to President Sadyr Japarov.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Build World's Longest Glass Suspension Bridge by 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to construct the world's longest glass suspension bridge, measuring 732 meters, in the Ala Archa National Park by the end of 2027. The project aims to be recognized in the Guinness Book of Records. This ambitious construction is expected to become a significant tourist attraction.
